label: EdgeSwitch 5 XP
description: EdgeSwitch 5 XP (ES-5XP) - five gigabit RJ45 ports with PoE configurable per port, plus a separate 10/100 management port. The small PoE switch in the EdgeSwitch XP line.
notes: Vendor figures from Ubiquiti techspecs (https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/wired/es-5xp, HTTP 200, 574,944 B, read 2026-11-20): "Networking interface: (5) 10/100/1000 Ethernet ports" and "Management interface: (1) 10/100 Ethernet port", so the management port is modelled at 100M and named separately from the five data ports. The PoE question this entry used to leave open - whether the ports were 802.3af/at or fixed-voltage passive - is answered on the vendor page: "PoE method: Passive", "PoE Out voltage range: 22-24V DC", "Max. PoE wattage per port: 11.5W" and "PoE configurable per port: Management port N/A, Data ports Off/24V". So the five data ports are 24 V passive PSE ports and are now classed `passive`, not `PoE`: 802.3af is a negotiated 48 V standard and this box does not speak it, which is the fault test/uisp-r-poe.test.js and test/ep-s16-poe.test.js were written for. No `poe` block: the page's only power figure is "Max. power consumption: 60W", which is the whole box including PoE output on a 24 V / 2.5 A adapter, so subtracting a box draw that the sheet never states would be invention - the position devices/ubiquiti/es-48-750w.json takes for the same reason. Five ports at the published 11.5 W per-port maximum would be 57.5 W of the 60 W supply, which is close enough that the adapter is worth knowing about when filling the box.
